key_insight: Centrosymmetric solids can generate dc photocurrents through coupling between light’s electric and magnetic fields, without requiring broken inversion symmetry.
engineering_relevance: The magnetoelectric bulk photovoltaic effect expands candidate materials for photodetection and could enable electrical readout of altermagnetic order.
method: Connect photocurrents to dipole moments of the Zeeman quantum metric and Zeeman Berry curvature.
Classify four injection-like and shift-like mechanisms by polarization and time-reversal symmetry.
Predict responses in centrosymmetric monolayer Pt₂HgSe₃ and altermagnetic RuF₄.
evidence_signal: The abstract predicts current densities on the order of 1 mA/m and sign reversal of RuF₄’s injection-like photocurrent when either light helicity or the Néel vector is switched.
watch_item: The reported responses are predictions; experimental validation and practical solar-cell efficiency are not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Magnetoelectric Bulk Photovoltaic Effect in Centrosymmetric Solids
